column1: # probes.tsv — the PROBE LEDGER (campaign #49). One row per probe, appended BEFORE the
# result is interpreted. A probe you did not log did not happen.
# Built by the convergence-metric implementation, Phase 1 of
#   date       ISO date the probe was run (YYYY-MM-DD).
#   gen        driver generation. Numeric for gen #1.. ; wNN for the pre-generation windows.
#   generator  the candidate generator that produced the probe. One of:
#              plus, FOR BACK-FILLED ROWS ONLY, `unknown` — the record does not name one.
#              `unknown` is a deliberate admission, not a default: a live row must never
#              use it. See NOTE ON BACK-FILL CONFIDENCE below.
#   candidate  short slug naming the thing probed.
#   verdict    LIVE | FAIL-CLOSED | VACUOUS | INCOMPLETE | OUT-OF-SCOPE
#                LIVE         a false claim was PROVED (or a security property violated).
#                FAIL-CLOSED  the hypothesis was refuted by measurement at HEAD.
#                VACUOUS      the positive control did not fire; THIS PROBE MEASURED NOTHING.
#                INCOMPLETE   priced/scoped but not run to a verdict.
#                OUT-OF-SCOPE CPython raises, or the construct is outside the value plane.
#   route      route number when verdict=LIVE, else `-`.
#   order      1 = first-order (the carrier predates the campaign)
#              2 = second-order (the carrier IS a campaign artefact: a repair, hardening,
#              `-` when verdict != LIVE, or when the record does not classify it.
#   note       free text. `backfill` marks a row reconstructed from prose rather than
#              logged live; such rows are LOWER CONFIDENCE and must stay separable.
# SCHEMA REFINEMENT FOUND BY THE PHASE-1 ACCEPTANCE TEST (recorded, not silently applied):
#   The first back-fill put two probes under OUT-OF-SCOPE because CPython raises on them,
#   and the acceptance test then under-counted the gen-#8 carve-out census (6 probes where
#   the handoff says 7). The record gives TWO facts about those probes -- they were RUN and
#   REFUSED, *and* CPython raises -- and the single `verdict` column had been made to carry
#   the wrong one. RULE, now applied uniformly:
#     `verdict` records what the MEASUREMENT returned. A probe that was run and refused is
#     FAIL-CLOSED even when CPython also raises; the raising is a note, because it bounds
#     how far the probe could have escalated, not whether it measured anything.
#     OUT-OF-SCOPE is reserved for candidates NEVER run against the plane (excluded by
#   This is the schema being fixed before further back-filling, exactly as Phase 1 requires.
# *** THE BACK-FILL IS ASYMMETRIC AND CROSS-GENERATION YIELD FROM IT IS NOT VALID. ***
#   The numerator (LIVE) was recoverable for EVERY route, because each has a route file and a
#   dated commit. The denominator (FAIL-CLOSED) was recoverable only where a generation wrote
#   a `PROBED ... NO FINDING` section. Generations that did not -- w49, 4, 11, 16, 17 -- come
#   out at or near 100 % yield, which is an artefact of the record, NOT a measurement. The
#   same defect makes `generator=unknown` read 35 LIVE / 0 FAIL-CLOSED.
#   THE ONLY ROWS SAFE TO COMPARE ACROSS GENERATIONS ARE THE `carve-out-census` ROWS, where
#   numerator and denominator came out of the SAME record. Everything else is a lower bound on
#   the denominator and therefore an UPPER bound on yield.
#   This is why the rule is "log before you interpret": from gen #18 on, rows are LIVE-logged
#   and this asymmetry disappears. Until then, quote back-filled yield only with this caveat.
# YIELD IS COMPUTED OVER `LIVE + FAIL-CLOSED` ONLY.
#   VACUOUS rows are instrument failures and are tracked SEPARATELY. A probe whose positive
#   control refused measured nothing; counting it as a clean negative would inflate the
#   denominator with non-measurements. This is route #94's shape (a guard whose population
#   is empty has checked nothing and looks exactly like a guard that passed) and it is the
#   campaign's standing vacuity rule applied to its own meta-level.
#   INCOMPLETE and OUT-OF-SCOPE rows are also excluded from yield.
# NOTE ON BACK-FILL CONFIDENCE (read before quoting any number from the back-filled rows):
#   Every row below carries note=backfill. They are reconstructed from
#   `date` for LIVE rows is HARD evidence (first commit mention, command above).
#   `gen` is taken from the handoff block that owns the section ("PROBED THIS GENERATION").
#   `generator` is recorded ONLY where the handoff names it; otherwise `unknown`.
#   Where a section reports a FAMILY of probes as one bullet ("NINE dunder carriers"),
#   one row is written and the note says how many carriers it covers. Those rows
#   UNDER-COUNT the denominator, which biases yield UP — the safe direction for a
#   convergence claim to be wrong in is DOWN, so treat back-filled yield as an UPPER bound.

The family census route #192's lesson demanded, widened to every DEFINITE stand-in for an UNKNOWN value. One hit: `_array_coerce_arg`'s `(Array.make 1 0)` — ROUTE #193. THE PLANE'S OWN BASELINE IS A ROUTE-FINDING SURFACE. Swept all fourteen entries of `bin/check-argument-coercion.py` with ONE probe — give the callee a contract that is TRUE of its own body and that READS the property the substitution changes, call it with the substituted-away shape, run CPython. THREE fell: #194 (`_coerce_to_int`'s array/map arms answered the literal `0`, and "the param is int-erased so no law reads it" is false — a contract on an int-erased param IS a law), #195 (the empty-list placeholder became `0` at an int-erased param; "the callee is a `\trusted` val with `ensures true`" is not a property of the callee, it is an assumption about it), #196 (the same placeholder is 1024 elements long at an `array int` param, and CPython's own answer was REFUSED). Nine hours, no emitter line changed since gen #29. The other eleven entries hold: the `materialize*` bridges carry BOTH a length law and a pointwise law; `any_map`/`any (array int)` are unconstrained; the option/union lifts recognise `pycsl_none` only; the `(Array.make 0 (IrOther ""))` arm is faithful for the same reason #196's repair is.

Same sweep on the sibling plane's ten entries. NO route: a generator expression in a VALUE position (`g == 0`, `g + 5`) and a bare `slice(0,2)` (`sl == 0`) both fail closed — route #41's per-name opaque fences the binding before the dict-shaped GenExp arm can be exploited, and the SliceExpr arm really is never reached in a value position. ONE STALE JUSTIFICATION FOUND AND CORRECTED: the `("_to_bool", '"Var"', "true")` entry still quoted the PRE-ROUTE-#55 rationale ("a sound OVER-approximation ... the real check is the `in` that follows") — the exact sentence route #55 refuted with witnesses 1104-1106. The CODE is right (the arm now fires only for a name the parent `&&` marked SUBSUMED, `if subst and name in subst:`, where `true` is faithful); the TEXT was the refuted one. A baseline entry that carries a justification a route already killed is the same hazard one level up.

`_to_bool` has TWO arms that answer the CONSTANT `true` for a guard whose Python answer can be False, each justified as "a sound over-approx for the type-safety+frame contract": the `_hvalmap_local_vars` map-truthiness arm (`if not vinfo:`) and the `_mutable_state_classes` + `svalue_of|object_of|sindex_of|arg0_of` optional-sub-node present-guard. An over-approximated GUARD makes the model take ONE branch always, which is unsound for ANY non-trivial `ensures` and unsound for `assigns` whenever the SKIPPED branch assigns something the taken one does not. MEASURED by instrumenting both arms and emitting all 53 mirror files: the `hvalmap` arm fires ZERO times — it is dead code in this tree — and the sub-node arm fires EXACTLY ONCE, in `ExpressionEmissionMixin._slice_array_or_opaque`. That method carries `#@ ensures True`, so no false postcondition is reachable; and its over-approximated guard (`self._expr_to_whyml(sl["lower"], …) if sl.get("lower") else "0"`) forces the MORE-assigning branch, so the frame claim is conservative in the right direction. SOUND AS WRITTEN, AND UNGATED: nothing stops a future conversion from putting a real `ensures` on a method that reaches these arms, or from adding an arm whose SKIPPED branch assigns. Recorded as a standing condition on the `check-type-keyed-constant-answers` entries rather than a new plane — population 1, and the check needs a full emission run.

The `_union_local_field_projection` entry in check-type-keyed-value-sentinels explicitly invited this: "the verdict is a TYPE ACCIDENT, not a guard ... if an `int`-carrier field read ever reaches this arm, re-measure it." RE-MEASURED: the int carrier DOES decide. `x: Optional[R] = None` then `return x.n` with `R.n: int` PROVES `ensures \result == 0` while CPython raises AttributeError — no type accident at int, the arm just answers the zero. NOT A ROUTE, because both exploitation paths are refused by fences that live ELSEWHERE: `except AttributeError` around the read is refused by route #174's dead-handler check (measured: the exact PIPELINE ERROR), and `#@ no_exception AttributeError` is refused at the directive because AttributeError is not a modelled exception (known set: IndexError, KeyError, StopIteration, ValueError, ZeroDivisionError). STANDING CONDITION now written into the entry: if AttributeError is ever added to the modelled set, this arm is immediately exploitable through `no_exception` and must be made opaque in the same increment.

The `(HInt 0)` entries in check-collapsed-option-reads asked for exactly this: "NOT re-measured by relaunch #51 and it should be, at the point where a `Dict[str, PyVal]` read is compared against a genuine `HInt 0`." Route #57 had also deliberately left the hval codomain on the SUBSCRIPT placeholder ("they were NOT measured, and route #56's lesson is that a carrier must be measured rather than assumed"). MEASURED, AND THE ANSWER SPLITS. CORPUS SIDE: not reachable — an int store into a `Dict[str, PyVal]` is an L3-tc error, so a genuine `HInt 0` cannot be put in the dict, and `isinstance(v, int)` on the read does not reach the `_pyval_locals` arm. The sentinel IS emitted (read in the generated WhyML: `| None -> (HInt 0)`), so it is live, just unreadable from ordinary Python. MIRROR SIDE, NOT CLOSED: the 53-file mirror emission contains 30 GENUINE `HInt i` constructions, so present-with-value-0 is constructible there and IS indistinguishable from absent. No mirror proof is yet shown to depend on the distinction, and none is shown not to. The entry now says "no reader found yet" rather than "collapsing-dead", and names the next step: find a mirror method whose contract distinguishes an absent key from a present 0.

`_handle_dotted_call`'s unmatched-instance tail types a call `array int` when the METHOD TAIL NAME is one of `encode`/`ljust`/`rjust`/`zfill` — route #110's exact shape (a guard keyed on a spelling that is also an ordinary Python identifier). Probed with user classes defining their own `encode` and `ljust` returning ints: both resolve as INSTANCE methods, so the arm does not fire, and both prove CPython's real answer. Where the arm DOES fire the decision is a TYPE, and a wrong type is a Why3 error rather than a wrong value; the downstream erasure it used to enable (an array actual reaching an int slot) is route #194's, already repaired. No route.

Route #140's shape on the ENSURES side rather than the `raises ... when` side: a callee `ensures \result == k` with `k: int = 5` called with the argument OMITTED, from a caller that has its own local `k = 99`. If the callee's clause rendered in the CALLER's scope the caller would derive `\result == 99`; CPython answers 5. BOTH shapes fail closed — the METHOD form dies with `unbound function or predicate symbol 'x0'` (a malformed but fail-closed emission) and the MODULE-LEVEL form emits a clean `let f (k: int) : int ensures { result = k }` with no leak and correctly leaves the false claim unproven.

The gen #28 ladder's suggested method — "grep Module 6 for every site that emits `()` for a whole statement" — done properly by AST rather than by grep: every statement handler in module6_whyml that returns an EMPTY emission list. TWO sites, both in `functions.py::_stmts_disp_writes`, which computes a WRITE SET and emits nothing by design. There is no erased-statement surface left in the statement handlers.

gen9 (four hand-picked READING callees — `is None`, `\length`, `in`, `\strlen` — crossed with bare ints, `None`, real values, empty and non-empty collections, a genexp through `sorted`, a comprehension and the OMITTED argument, four wrong claims each) COMPLETE over 8 seeds: 112 programs, every one running under CPython first, ZERO false proofs. The surface routes #192/#194/#195/#196 came from is clean after their repairs.

The generalization of the `--reverify-proofs` find: enumerate every `--flag` pycsl.py defines and diff against what any bin/ script, the Makefile or a test-suite runner actually passes. 14 of 31 are never passed. Most are options (`--prover`, `--timelimit`, proof paths), but FOUR are opt-in SOUNDNESS checks nothing exercises: `--check-behavioral-subtyping`, `--strict-concurrent-checks`, `--strict-no-exception-propagation`, `--soundness-report`. `--reverify-proofs` was the fifth and is now gated.

Why does nothing run `--check-behavioral-subtyping` (Layer D: `pre_base ==> pre_sub`, `post_sub ==> post_base` for overrides)? Because the DEFAULT mode refuses the shapes it would check. Probed both Liskov carriers with a base `A` (`ensures \result == 1`) and an override `B` (`ensures \result == 2`), CPython answering 2 in each: the DIRECT call `B().f()` claiming `\result == 1` is UNKNOWN — dispatch is faithful, routes #123/#125's repairs hold — and the POLYMORPHIC call through a base-annotated parameter (`def use(a: A)` called with a `B`) is an L3-tc TYPE ERROR (`has type b, but is expected to have type a`): PyCSL does not model subtype substitution at a record param at all, so there is no place for an LSP violation to be answered wrongly. Fail-closed, not unsound.

A class with NO fields (no `__init__`, or an `__init__` that sets nothing) instantiated as a local emits `let b = {  } in` — an EMPTY RECORD LITERAL, which is a Why3 SYNTAX ERROR, so the whole file is refused. FAIL-CLOSED, and it cost nothing here (adding one field to the base made both Liskov probes run). Recorded because the failure MODE is wrong: this is a MALFORMED EMISSION, not a refusal with a reason, and the campaign's own distinction is that a refusal must say what it refused and why. Route #97 (`Liskov goal dropped for a fieldless base`) is the same class of object. No corpus file has the shape, so no gate sees it.

`--strict-no-exception-propagation` is off by default, and in default mode `_wrap_unannotated_call_with_strict_assert` returns the bare call — so a `no_exception`-enabled function calling an ABSTRACT or UNANNOTATED callee gets NO obligation from that wrapper. Probed the two carriers that would exploit it: a `no_exception ValueError` function calling (a) a same-file UNANNOTATED callee that raises ValueError, and (b) a `\trusted` callee that raises it. CPython raises in both. BOTH FAIL CLOSED — Why3 itself rejects them ("this expression raises unlisted exception ValueError"), so routes #178/#182's repairs are what hold the line and the strict flag would only add pessimism, not soundness. No route.

`bin/check-yield-erasure.py` scopes itself to CONVERTED MIRROR functions (`MIRROR = src/self-annotate/src`) and states the lowering plainly: "a `yield` statement lowers to `let _ = 0 in ()` — the yielded expression is evaluated for nothing and discarded". So: is a CORPUS generator the same hole? Probed two consumers of a two-value generator — summing it in a `for`, and `len(list(gen()))` — with claims of 0 where CPython answers 3 and 2. BOTH FAIL CLOSED with a TYPE error ("This expression has type (), but is expected to have type int"): the generator `def` emits `unit`, which is symptom (1) the plane itself names, and in the corpus that mismatch is a REFUSAL rather than a silent erasure. The plane is right to scope itself to the mirror, where a converted function's CALLERS can be typed to accept the unit.

`bin/check-dropped-mutation.py`'s TRYFINAL bucket is an ADMITTED fail-open with its own ratchet: Module 6's `_handle_try_stmt` reads `stmt.body` and `stmt.handlers` and neither `orelse` nor `finalbody`, and "Python runs `finally` on EVERY exit path". #33 emits the `finally` only in the ONE case expressible by appending it (no handlers, no `raise` in the lowered body). Probed the three shapes OUTSIDE that case, each with a claim FALSE of CPython (which answers 2): a no-handler `try/finally` (the handled case — correctly REFUSES the false claim), a `try/except/finally` (a PIPELINE ERROR with an explicit diagnostic naming the measurement that motivated it), and a `try/except/else` (unproven). ALL THREE FAIL CLOSED. The residue is fenced by a refusal, not silently dropped.

`bin/check-param-mutator-visibility.py` names its own gap: "only through a plain function call, and only with the collection reaching the callee as a bare parameter. A mutation through a NESTED data structure, through a METHOD ON `self`, or through an ALIAS bound inside the callee is outside this table." Probed the two not already covered by a route (self-field mutation is route #13, caller-side aliasing is route #59), each with the plane's own decisive shape — the callee mutates, the caller asserts UNCHANGED, CPython answers 1: a NESTED `List[List[int]]` with `m[0].append(1)`, a callee-local ALIAS `b = a; b.append(1)`, and a `Dict[str, List[int]]` with `d["k"].append(1)`. ALL THREE FAIL CLOSED — the first two on a TYPE error (`seq int` where `int` is expected), the third undecided. The table's uncovered shapes are uncovered because they do not reach a lowering that can answer them, not because they answer wrongly.

`bin/check-avatar-frame-parity.py` records "CENSUS at #33: 11 of 476 `\trusted` stubs have no `#@ assigns`" — the THIRD kind of silent frame hole, and the one that "cost no marker to fix". RE-MEASURED under the campaign's own re-measure-never-inherit rule: STILL EXACTLY 11, AND THE SAME ELEVEN (errors.py message/as_dict; module6_whyml/statements.py _resolve_dotted_signature, _is_emit_ir_expr, _coerce_to_int, _expr_to_whyml_string_ctx, _is_string_expr, _e, _maybe_emit_no_exception_assert, _mutex_inv_application; module6_whyml/stmt_control_flow.py _coerce_to_int), with the denominator now 459 markers rather than 476. The plane's text is updated in place with the re-measurement. A NOTE ON MEASURING IT, paid for on my first attempt: a census walking from the `#@` block to the `def` must skip PLAIN `#` COMMENT LINES as well as blanks and decorators, or six of the eleven come back unnamed and the count reads 17 — a census that cannot name its members is not a measurement.

The (B) INHERITED bucket (11 frameless avatars for mixin methods declared in another mirror file) is a REAL self-TCB residue, and its two reopening routes are already priced by relaunch #33: ROUTE 1 measured 0 of 53 mirrors moved (nothing to find), ROUTE 2 REFUTED on CORRECTNESS grounds (the coarse `writes { _pyobj_state }` forces a source declaration that is FALSE IN THE OTHER DIRECTION for a pure callee — exactly the over-claiming #32 refused). What remains is the source-level protocol-stub route, which the plane itself says to "budget as a SEGMENT, not as an increment": one marker per stub (RAISING the trust metric 459 -> 470), a caller fixpoint of 5-6 iterations per file, and a whole-file re-proof of each. NOT started in gen #30's remaining window rather than left half-built at the deadline — the rule is never leave an unverified tree. The census above is the part that was bounded, and it is done.

RE-MEASURED the (B) INHERITED bucket rather than inheriting relaunch #33's figure: it is SEVEN, not 11, across FIVE distinct methods — `_py_stmts_to_ir` (3 sites: frontend/__init__, frontend/ir_resolve, pycsl; declared in frontend/Module5_IREmitter), `_materialize_bridge` (expressions; declared in statements), `_collect_array_var_assigns` (functions; declared in types), `_is_emit_ir_expr` and `_is_string_expr` (functions; declared in expressions). CHECKED THE CHEAP PATH AND IT IS NOT AVAILABLE: the plane notes that three of four earlier closures were the "trusted stub with no `#@ assigns`" kind and "cost no marker to fix", so I checked whether any of the SEVEN inheriting mirrors already carries a stub of its method — NONE DOES (0 of 7). Closing (B) therefore costs SEVEN NEW MARKERS (459 -> 466, against the metric this campaign exists to lower), plus the caller fixpoint #32 measured at 5-6 iterations per file, plus a whole-file re-proof of five mirrors per iteration — and one of them is `module6_whyml/expressions` at 8250s, so a single fixpoint over that file is ~12h on its own. Deferred with the numbers, not with a shrug: it is a SEGMENT, and starting it inside gen #30's remaining window would leave an unverified tree at the deadline.

Third re-measure of check-dropped-mutation's founding sweep: the `#@` annotation half. The gate records "MODULE 5, CSL annotation handlers (`_csl_*`, 79 of them, against the node classes in `Module2_Parser.py`): ZERO drop a field." `_IRNODE_CTORS` maps CSL-AST class NAMES (`ProofDecl`, `ClassInvariant`, `RaisesDecl`, ...) to `emit_ir` ADT constructors, gated on `@mutable_state`, and justifies itself with "Corpus-inert: no corpus program declares a @mutable_state class". THE GATE IS USER-REACHABLE: `_is_mutable_state_decorated` keys on the DECORATOR NAME ONLY, so a user who writes their own no-op `def mutable_state(c): return c` and decorates a class with it turns the whole table on -- this is route #110's spelling-collision shape. The run FAILS with a Why3 TYPE ERROR ("expected to have type PyCSL_Program.proofdecl") -- the ADT application does not type against the per-class record. FAIL-CLOSED AND LOUD. Note the reason differs from the one written: the comment credits "bound BY NAME, so a payload/field-order mismatch can never silently mis-bind", but what actually stops THIS shape is the type clash, not the name binding.

`_to_bool` carries two arms that answer the CONSTANT `true` for a container guard, each justified as a sound over-approximation and one of them MEASURED DEAD in this tree. No false collapse in either the symbolic or the literal direction.

column5: My route #200 refusal walks node['args'] ONLY. The IR carries keyword actuals in a SEPARATE slot: {'type':'Call','func':'callee','args':[],'keywords':[{'arg':'p','value':{'type':'String',...}}]}. So callee(p="a") against a DECLARED 'p: int' still PROVES \result == 1 while CPython answers 2 -- the same route, in the spelling the repair did not run. Found by applying gen #30's own lesson (i) to my own fix, one hour after writing it. The #202 patch now covers positional AND keyword actuals.

column8: Question 2 turned on my OWN #202 gate: which other ACTUAL SLOTS exist besides `args` and `keywords`? Probed both. `callee(*xs)` with `xs = ["a"]` against a declared `p: int` whose contract reads `p`: REFUSED (a starred actual lowers to the bare inner value and does not reach the hash). `callee(**d)`: see the line below. Neither spelling reaches the substitution, so the gate's two slots are the two that matter.

`callee(**d)` with `d = {"p": "a"}` against the same declared `p: int`: REFUSED by an ARITY diagnostic ("passes 0 positional argument(s) but parameter 'p' has ..."), before any coercion can happen. So the two actual slots the #202 gate walks (positional `args` and `keywords`) are the only two that reach the hash substitution, and that is measured rather than assumed.

column5: `s = f"{n}"` with n = 5 emits `s := !n` -- the f-string IS the integer it interpolates. Then `s == "5"` compares `5 = 1359629258` (the hash of the string literal) and DECIDES FALSE, so \result == 2 PROVES while CPython answers 1 (`f"{5}" == "5"` is True). TRUE twin \result == 1 REFUSED. Route #199 repaired the EMPTY-parts arm of the same function; this is the LEGACY int-hash arm one branch down -- question 2 (which other arm of the same function reaches the same answer) again. The mirror's `_handle_fstring_expr` is a re-trusted STUB, so the live method may declare an abstract op without any frame or verbatim-mirror cost.

column8: Question 2 applied across route #203's FAMILY rather than its function: which OTHER int->string conversions could return the integer raw? `s = str(n)` with n = 5 then `s == "5"`, claiming the answer CPython does NOT give: REFUSED. `s = "%d" % n`: see the next line. Only the SINGLE-PART f-string returned its operand unwrapped; the other two conversions already go through an opaque (`int_to_string` / `str_mod_op`).

`s = "%d" % n` with n = 5 then `s == "5"`, claiming CPython's non-answer: REFUSED. Together with the `str(n)` line above, the int->string family is closed: only the SINGLE-PART f-string (route #203) returned its operand unwrapped, and it now answers a value-keyed opaque like the other two.

Question 1 (which SPELLING did the repair not run?) applied to route #203's own fix, before anyone else could: `f"{n:d}"` (format spec) and `f"{n!r}"` (conversion) are the two other single-interpolation spellings. BOTH REFUSED after the repair, each claiming the answer CPython does not give. So the `len(parts) == 1` scope covers all three spellings of a single-interpolation f-string, and that is measured rather than argued from the AST shape.

The other two STRING BUILDERS, probed with the answer CPython does not give: `",".join(["a","b"])` compared against "a,b" -- REFUSED; `"ab" + "cd"` compared against "abcd" -- see the next line. Neither builder returns an operand raw the way route #203's single-part f-string did.

`a = "ab"; b = "cd"; s = a + b` then `s == "abcd"`, with the claim CPython does NOT give: REFUSED -- so no false proof. Worth noting the OTHER direction is also unprovable here, i.e. this is a COMPLETENESS gap rather than a clean win: the string-model `str_concat_op` carries `ensures result = concat a b`, so the true answer ought to be reachable, and is not in this shape. Sound, recorded, NOT a route; a completeness item for whoever next touches the string model.

The strongest form of question 3 available: `check-argument-coercion.py` calls the string hash "injective-by-luck only", and `stable_hash` is a 32-bit function, so a collision is FINDABLE. FOUND ONE in 71382 candidates (a few seconds): `stable_hash('"ah02"') == stable_hash('"atc3"') == 185314078`. Then probed the three places a collision could DECIDE something, each claiming the answer CPython does not give (the two strings are different, so all three tests are False in Python): a direct comparison `a == b`; `"atc3" in {"ah02": 1}` (dict key); `"atc3" in {"ah02"}` (set member). ALL THREE REFUSED -- string equality and membership go through the REAL Why3 string model (`str_eq_op`), not the int-hash domain, so the collision never reaches a decision. "Injective-by-luck" is a fair description of the HASH, but the hash is not what decides string equality; route #200/#202's exploit needed a contract naming the integer, which is a different and now-closed path. Recorded with the collision itself so nobody has to re-find it.

The assignment-side companion to the return-boundary enumeration: every STRING CONSTANT assigned to the value variable inside `_handle_assign_stmt`, `_handle_fieldassign_stmt` and `_emit_first_assign`. SEVEN sites. `val = "0"` for a Tuple/SetLit literal and `val = "1"/"0"` for True/False are already probed (the first fail-closed via route #41's per-name device, the second FAITHFUL). `(const (None: option int))`, `(any_map ())` (route #86's repair) and `pycsl_none_str` are opaques or faithful empties. The one DEFINITE non-opaque left is `val = '(IrOther "")'` for a `None` assigned to an emit_ir local -- but it is gated on `@mutable_state` AND on `_emit_ir_local_vars`, i.e. the emitter's own model, and the user-reachable route to `@mutable_state` was probed separately this window and fails closed by a Why3 TYPE ERROR. So the assignment side is enumerated, not sampled.

Question 1 applied to route #199's FAMILY (empty literals, not just the empty f-string): `b = b""` then `len(b) == 0` and `s = ""` then `len(s) == 0`, each claiming the answer CPython does NOT give (both are 1 in Python). BOTH REFUSED -- no false proof. Both are also COMPLETENESS gaps in the other direction (the true length-0 fact is not provable either), which is worth recording next to the concat item above: the string/bytes length model is sound and thin.

SEVEN integer operations whose lowerings could DECIDE a comparison wrongly, each asserted with a value CPython does not produce: `5 & 3`, `5 | 2`, `5 ^ 3`, `1 << 4`, `16 >> 2`, `2 ** 10` and `-8 >> 1` (the sign-sensitive one, where a logical-shift model would give a huge positive). ALL SEVEN REFUSED. Note this is also a COMPLETENESS statement about the bit-op model: the true values are not provable either, so these operations are uninterpreted rather than wrongly interpreted -- sound, thin, and recorded alongside the string-concat and empty-length items.

Two list BUILDERS whose result length a wrong model could decide, each claiming `len(...) == 0` where CPython gives 3 and 3: `[0] * 3` and `[1,2] + [3]`. BOTH REFUSED. This is the same family as route #193/#196/#201 (a built collection whose LENGTH the model claims to know) probed on the two builders those routes did not touch.

Route #97's family (behavioural subtyping) probed on the two shapes that would show a WRONG DISPATCH rather than a dropped goal. Direct: `class B(A)` overriding `f`, `b = B(); b.f()` claiming the BASE's answer 1 -- CPython gives 2. REFUSED. Upcast: the same B passed to `def call_as_a(a: A) -> int: return a.f()` whose own contract claims 1, then the caller claims 1 -- CPython gives 2 through the same path. REFUSED. So neither the direct call nor the upcast lets the base's contract decide for a derived receiver.

The bluntest possible soundness hole, checked rather than assumed: is there a user-writable ASSUME? `#@ assume 1 == 2` before a `return 1` under `#@ ensures \result == 99` is REFUSED at the parser ("unrecognized contract keyword"). Cross-checked against `test-suite/annotations.md`: the only assumption surfaces in the language are `#@ \trusted` (counted by the trust metric this campaign exists to lower), `#@ assumes bounded_int(N)` (a typing directive, not a free assumption) and `#@ fresh_globals` (Module4-enforced to an entry point, and proof-backed by the constructor's own `ensures`). So the trust surface is ENUMERABLE and has no back door, which is what makes the `\trusted` count meaningful as a metric.

A loop that the model thinks RAN when Python skips it entirely would be the loop-boundary analogue of this generation's value-boundary routes. Probed both spellings of a zero-iteration loop, each claiming the body ran once (`c == 1`) where CPython leaves `c == 0`: `for i in range(0)` and `for i in range(-3)`. BOTH REFUSED. The empty-loop case does not decide the wrong way.

Route #193's family (a BUILT collection whose length the model claims to know) probed on the two comprehension builders it did not touch: `[i for i in range(3)]` and `{"a": i for i in range(3)}`, each claiming `len(...) == 0` where CPython gives 3 and 1. BOTH REFUSED. With the list-repetition / list-concatenation pair above, every collection BUILDER reachable from a user program has now been probed for a decided-wrong length this window.

`check-dropped-mutation`'s founding finding was a MULTI-TARGET assign (`a = b = 5` dropped `b`, and a three-line program with a FALSE postcondition reported Verification SUCCESS). Probed the two sibling shapes that drop a binding the same way if they are mishandled: `a, b = 1, 2` then claiming `a == 2` (CPython: a is 1), and the SWAP `a, b = b, a` then claiming `a == 1` (CPython: a is 2 after the swap - a naive sequential lowering would give exactly the claimed 1). BOTH REFUSED. The swap is the sharper of the two: it is the shape where a left-to-right assignment order, rather than Python's simultaneous one, produces a DIFFERENT answer instead of an unknown.

The two list mutations that SHRINK a collection, i.e. the shapes where a model that kept the old length would DECIDE a length test wrongly: `del xs[0]` and `xs.pop()`, each claiming `len(xs) == 3` after the mutation where CPython gives 2. BOTH REFUSED WITH AN EXPLICIT DIAGNOSTIC rather than a failed proof -- "`del xs[...]` on a non-dict/set receiver is not modelled" and "`xs.pop(...)` MUTATES its receiver in place, and no certified lowering...". That is the fail-CLOSED direction done properly: a shape with no sound lowering is REFUSED by name, so it cannot silently keep a stale length.

GHOST CODE is by construction a place where a specification variable could leak into the real program's model. Two probes: (a) a ghost assignment `#@ ghost g = 99` alongside `r = 1`, claiming `\result == 99` -- REFUSED, so the ghost value does not become the result; (b) a ghost assignment that SHADOWS A REAL LOCAL, `r = 1` then `#@ ghost r = 99`, with the postcondition reading `r == 99` -- REFUSED, so a ghost write does not overwrite the real local the contract reads. The ghost plane is isolated in both directions.

The classic Hoare-logic hole: a callee with `#@ requires False` proves ANY postcondition of itself vacuously, so if a CALLER could use that postcondition without discharging the precondition, every program would be provable. Probed directly: `def callee(p: int) -> int: return 1` with `requires False` / `ensures \result == 99`, called as `return callee(0)` under `ensures \result == 99` (CPython answers 1). REFUSED -- the caller must establish `False` and cannot. The call-site precondition obligation is real, which is the premise every route in this campaign that exploits a CALLEE CONTRACT depends on.

Six more shapes, each asserted with the answer CPython does NOT give: `d.get("a", 7)` on a PRESENT key claiming the default 7 (CPython 5); `4 in [1,2,3]`; `isinstance(5, (str, bytes))` -- the TUPLE-of-types form; a field store `c.n = 9` then claiming the constructor's 0; a module GLOBAL read claiming 99 where the module sets 1; and a NESTED CLOSURE reading an enclosing local. FIVE REFUSED; the nested closure is REFUSED WITH A DIAGNOSTIC (the hard-refusal class), which matches the gen-29 record that a nested closure is a named refusal rather than a silent drop. The `d.get` case is the sharpest of the six: it is the PRESENT-key twin of the absent-key probe earlier this window, and the model does not answer the default for a key it has.

The strongest frame probe available: a method DECLARING `#@ assigns self.a` whose body ALSO writes `self.b`, and a caller that reads `k.b` after the call and claims the constructor's 0 (CPython: 2, because the body really did write it). REFUSED. So an under-declared `assigns` does not let a caller keep a stale field value -- the frame obligation is real on both sides of the call, which matters because every route this generation that exploits a CALLEE CONTRACT relies on the caller's side of the contract being sound.

A class carrying `#@ class invariant self.n >= 0` with a method whose OWN contract says `ensures self.n == -5` -- i.e. a method that provably breaks the invariant -- and a caller reading the broken value. REFUSED. The invariant is CHECKED at the method boundary rather than merely assumed there, which is the direction that matters: an invariant assumed-but-not-checked is a `requires False` in disguise and would make every method of the class vacuous.

The `#@ no_exception` directive is an OBLIGATION, and a directive that is parsed but not enforced would make every implicit-exception VC vacuous. Two probes where the exception is plainly reachable: `#@ no_exception IndexError` over `return xs[10]` with no length precondition, and `#@ no_exception ZeroDivisionError` over `return 10 // d` with `d` unconstrained. BOTH FAIL. The obligation is discharged, not assumed.

The STORE twin of routes #200/#202: a string literal written into a container the annotation types as int-valued, then read back and compared against the string's computable hash. `xs: List[int] = [0]; xs[0] = "a"; xs[0] == 976090257` and `d: Dict[str,int] = {}; d["k"] = "a"; d["k"] == 976090257`, both claiming the hash where CPython has the string. BOTH REFUSED. With the field-store probe earlier this window, all three STORE positions (element, dict value, field) are closed against the nameable-hash device; only the ARGUMENT position ever reached it, and that is now refused at Module 4.

Re-probed the bytes model at the gen #30 final HEAD, since routes #199/#203 changed how a non-int value reaches the int domain and `v69`/`v70` (the value-differential drivers for bytes indexing) predate that: `b = b"ab"` then `b[0] == 0` (CPython 97) and `len(b) == 0` (CPython 2), each claiming the answer CPython does not give. BOTH REFUSED. The f-string repairs did not open the bytes path.

A `\forall` postcondition over a range the body only PARTLY establishes: `ensures \forall i; 0 <= i and i < n ==> a[i] == 0` with n == 3 and a body that writes a[0] and a[1] but not a[2]. FAILS. A quantified postcondition that discharged on a partial body would be the single most dangerous hole in the language, since every array contract in the corpus is of that shape; it does not.

A surface this campaign has a SKILL for and no GATE: the 93 `src/pycsl_lib/` stubs are body-verified re-implementations of stdlib modules, so a contract can be perfectly proven OF ITS OWN BODY and still be wrong ABOUT PYTHON. Built a differential harness ($SCRATCH/stdlib_diff.py) mapping 20 stub packages to their real modules and comparing 73 functions on ~800 type-domain-valid inputs. THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS MISLEADING AND THAT IS THE FINDING: 129 "mismatches", and every one inspected is the stub being an ABSTRACTION rather than a re-implementation -- `mth.comb(6,3)` returns 6 where CPython returns 20, but its contract only claims `\result >= 1`, which is TRUE of CPython; `mth.fabs(-19)` returns -19, but its contract carries `requires x >= 0` and my harness violated it. `bsect` (the one package that IS a faithful re-implementation) compared 8000 inputs against `bisect` with ZERO mismatches. SO: body equality is NOT the soundness criterion for these stubs; CONTRACT-TRUTH-OF-CPYTHON is, and it is a different and harder check. Recorded with the harness so the next window can build the right instrument instead of re-deriving the wrong one. Spot-checked three value-asserting contracts against CPython by hand -- `b64.b16encode_len(n) == n*2`, `b64.b16decode_len(n) == n//2`, `sysmod.get_float_info_max_10_exp() == 308` -- all THREE TRUE.

Built the instrument the previous row said was needed: `scratchpad/g30/stdlib_contract_diff.py` parses each stub's `#@ requires`/`#@ ensures`, generates inputs SATISFYING the requires, runs the REAL stdlib function and evaluates the ensures against CPython's answer. 2000 contract checks over 12 packages; **21 VIOLATIONS in 2 functions**. (a) `mth.remainder(x: int, y: int)` -- `requires x >= 0, y > 0`, `ensures \result >= 0 and \result < y`, body `return x % y`, docstring "IEEE 754-style remainder ... For integers, same as x % y". THE DOCSTRING IS FALSE: `math.remainder(8,5)` is -2.0 (round-to-NEAREST) while `8 % 5` is 3 (FLOOR), so the contract is false of the function the RST citation names. (b) `stat.filemode(mode: int) -> str` -- `ensures \result == "----------"` with a body returning exactly that constant, while `stat.filemode(2)` is '?-------w-'. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED AFTER CHECKING THE IMPORT PATH: `import_classifier._stub_set` collects only the `.py` STEMS directly under `src/pycsl_lib/`, and there is NO name map from `math` to `mth`, so a user's `import math` does NOT pick up these contracts -- the stubs are standalone modules whose contracts are true of their own bodies. So these are DOCUMENTATION/NAMING fidelity defects, not proof-soundness holes. Recorded at the honest severity, with the census that frames them: **124 of 870 pycsl_lib functions (14.3%) have a single-constant-return body**.

`check-dropped-mutation`'s DANGLING bucket is a HARD 0 for a `#@` block with nothing after it (measured: a trailing `#@ ensures \result == 99` after a function returning 1 once reported Verification SUCCESS). Probed the two shapes that would drop a contract the same way WITHOUT being dangling: a BLANK LINE between the `#@ ensures` and the `def`, and an ORDINARY COMMENT between them. Both carry `ensures \result == 99` over a body returning 1, so a silent drop would report SUCCESS. BOTH FAIL -- the contract is still attached across a blank line and across a comment, so neither gap silently discards it.

The two loop exits whose mishandling produces a WRONG DECISION rather than an unknown: a `break` (the model must not conclude the loop ran to completion) and a `continue` (the model must not conclude every iteration reached the tail). Probed with claims FALSE of CPython: a loop breaking at i==3 then claiming `i == 10` (CPython leaves i at 3), and a loop with a `continue` at i==2 then claiming the tail ran 4 times (CPython runs it 3). BOTH REFUSED.

`#@ lemma` declares a function to be "a PROVED logical fact" that other proofs may cite via `#@ uses`. A lemma accepted with a FALSE conclusion would be the single widest hole in the language, since a cited false fact discharges anything. Probed directly: `#@ lemma` / `#@ requires True` / `#@ ensures 1 == 2` over an empty body. FAILS. The lemma's own conclusion is discharged like any other postcondition, not assumed.

The opt-in escape hatch, probed so the ledger records what it actually does rather than what the docs say it does: a `#@ \trusted reviewer: probe` function with `ensures \result == 99` and a body returning 1, called by a caller claiming 99. PROVES -- CPython answers 1. THAT IS THE DOCUMENTED, OPT-IN MECHANISM, not a route: a `\trusted` body is not verified and its contract is an AXIOM, which is exactly why the marker count (459) is the campaign's headline metric and why `bin/check-value-differential.py` ships a NEGATIVE TEST built on this very shape (`negative-test/n01_trusted_assumption_is_red.py`). Recorded here because a ledger that lists only the closed holes, and never the one deliberately-open door, misrepresents the perimeter.

Route #29 fenced the four ARRAY SPEC ATOMS under the heap models (`typed`/`store`) because their lowerings erased to a literal there. The ORDINARY array postcondition under those same models had not been probed this generation. `a[0] = 6` with `#@ ensures a[0] == 5` and an honest `#@ assigns a[0..0]`, run under ALL THREE models: FAILS under `typed`, FAILS under `store`, FAILS under `hoare`. So the heap models' element-store semantics are not erased the way the spec atoms were -- the #29 fence is around the atoms specifically, and the plain read/write path is sound in all three.

Route #197 closed the UNKNOWN-typed `getattr` DEFAULT. The write side had not been probed this generation: a `setattr(k, "n", 9)` and a plain `k.n = 7`, each followed by a read claiming the CONSTRUCTOR's 0 -- so a DROPPED store would report SUCCESS (the `check-dropped-mutation` shape, at the field). BOTH REFUSED. Neither write is silently discarded.

The sharpest form of the facade shape, censused by name: a function whose body is a SINGLE CONSTANT RETURN **and** whose contract PINS that same constant -- verified, computing nothing, and claiming exactly the nothing it computes. **TWELVE across the whole of `src/pycsl_lib/`**: ten in `os/__init__.py` (`getcwd`, `get_exec_path`, `chflags`, `confstr`, `copy_file_range`, `getxattr`, `listxattr`, `_kill`, `islink`, `is_junction`, all `-> 0`), one in `stat` (`filemode -> "----------"`, now relabelled) and one in `sysmod`. Sound TODAY for the same reason as every other stub -- the contract is true of the body and nothing substitutes it for the real module -- and it is precisely the set that turns FALSE the day something does: a proof that `islink(p) == 0` is a proof that nothing is ever a symlink. NOT COVERED BY `bin/check-stdlib-contract-fidelity.py` and cannot be: `os` is on that gate's SAFETY deny-list because the gate CALLS the real function, and `os.chflags` with a generated argument is not a test. Recorded BY NAME so the `agent-stdlib-annotate` owner has the list rather than the number.

Route #30's shape (`_match_pattern_cond` fell through to the constant `true`, so `case [1,2]:` on an int TOOK THE ARM) re-probed at the gen #30 HEAD on the simplest spelling: `match x` with `x = 5`, `case 1` claiming \result == 1 where CPython takes `case _` and answers 2. REFUSED. The pattern condition still decides correctly, and `check-singleton-constant-lowering` still carries the `_match_pattern_cond` / `"Wildcard"` / `true` entry as its justified constant (a wildcard REALLY does always match).

Followed the campaign's headline metric into the layer I had just gated and found the metric does not reach it. `src/pycsl_lib/` carries TWO `#@ \trusted` markers: (a) `mth.isqrt`, `reviewer: newton-method-variant`, with a STATED reason (the Newton variant needs nonlinear arithmetic beyond Alt-Ergo) and a contract (`requires x >= 0`, `ensures \result >= 0`) that is TRUE of `math.isqrt` -- honest; (b) `hlib.Sha256.update`, a BARE `#@ \trusted` with NO reviewer and NO reason, in a class whose `hexdigest` returns `[0] * 64` under `ensures \length(\result) == 64` -- i.e. an all-zero digest behind a length-only contract. NEITHER IS GATED: `bin/check-trusted-reasons.py` scopes to the MIRROR root `src/self-annotate/src` and `bin/count-trusted-directives.py` globs `MIRROR/**/*.py`, so the 459 headline count EXCLUDES `pycsl_lib` entirely. The skill `agent-stdlib-annotate` says this layer should carry ZERO `\trusted` and that an irreducibly-opaque kernel "becomes an abstract `val` pinned by a cited proof -- never `\trusted`". So the rule exists, the violations exist, and no plane connects them.

A check that is not in a runner is not a gate, applied to the stdlib layer's OTHER stated policy. `config/skills/agent-stdlib-annotate/SKILL.md` item 4: "**Every stub ships a property-proving `<mod>_demo.py`.** ... This is a **policy**, not a suggestion". MEASURED: **93 stub packages, 13 demos**, and all 13 live under `attic/pycsl_lib/` -- i.e. the ATTIC, not beside the stubs they prove (ast, bisect, collections, dataclasses, enum, functools, heapq, io, math, os, re, sys, typing). NOTHING RUNS THEM: neither `bin/run-reference-tests.sh` nor `bin/run-soundness-planes.sh` mentions `_demo`; the only file in `bin/` that does is `cmmi-mod-index.py`, an indexer. So the policy is stated as non-negotiable, satisfied for 14% of the layer, and the artefacts that DO exist are in the attic and unexercised. Recorded as a NAMED gap for the `agent-stdlib-annotate` owner: either the demos move back and get a runner, or the policy is rewritten to say what is actually enforced. NOT gated this window -- building a runner for 13 attic drivers is a judgement about where they belong, not a measurement.

Lesson (e) -- "a check that is not in a runner is not a gate" -- re-measured at the gen #30 final HEAD. Earlier this generation the same census found FIVE uncollected gates (`check-trusted-reasons.py` among them, a full plane with a ratchet that NOTHING ran). NOW: **48 `bin/check-*` scripts, 47 named in `bin/run-soundness-planes.sh`**, and the one that is not -- `check-self-annotate-sync.sh` -- is a THIN WRAPPER whose entire body is `python3 check-self-annotate-mirror-sync.py`, and that script IS in the runner. So the uncollected-gate class is CLOSED: every instrument in `bin/` is either in the battery or an alias for something that is.

The mirror carries the `#@` annotations and the live emitter is meant to be un-annotated; an annotation that LEAKED into `src/pycsl/` would be read as a real contract wherever the mirror imports that module. CENSUSED: **12 `#@` lines across 6 live files**, and every one checked by hand. Eleven are inside DOCSTRINGS or COMMENTS -- agent prompts that describe the syntax (`agent-infer-invariants`, `agent-invariant-writer`), a route #33 worked example in `desugar.py` explicitly labelled "<-- FALSE OF THE PROGRAM", emitted-WhyML samples in `stmt_control_flow`, and two `#@ requires_method` documentation lines in `expressions`. The twelfth is REAL and DELIBERATE: `errors.py` carries `#@ class invariant self.line >= 0` on `PyCSLError`, documented in that module's own docstring as a "Self-annotation seed (StdlibCoverage workplan PR 9, §9.1)" -- `errors` is imported BY the mirror (the pipeline logs "Imported class from 'errors': PyCSLSemanticError"), so the annotation is where it has to be. No leakage.

Lesson (e) applied to the CORPUS instead of to `bin/`. `test-suite/corpus/` has four subdirectories; `bin/run-reference-tests.sh` hard-codes exactly TWO (`PYCSL_DIR` = pycsl-reference, `PYTHON_DIR` = python-reference) and `bin/byte-diff-sweep.sh` globs pycsl-reference plus a pyref pass. **`test-suite/corpus/negative/` is in NEITHER**, and it holds three witnesses (`neg_001_wrong_postcondition`, `neg_002_broken_invariant`, `neg_003_precondition_violation`) with NO `# pycsl-expected:` marker between them. Ran all three by hand at HEAD: 001 and 002 FAIL (as their names promise); **003 PROVES**, and that is CORRECT -- its contracts (`requires x > 0` / `ensures \result > 0` over `return x * 2`) are true, and the "violation" is a `needs_positive(-1)` call inside an `if __name__ == "__main__":` block, i.e. a DYNAMIC-ORACLE test, not a static one. So no hole -- but three witnesses sit outside every runner with no expectation recorded, which is exactly the shape that let route #42 reopen under a green byte-diff. FIX = give them `# pycsl-expected:` markers and a runner, or move them where a runner already looks.

Route #90 class re-probed: a refusal whose own REMEDIATION ADVICE, if followed, yields an UNSOUND program. The sampler states this is mechanically unreachable ("no program-level sampler can see English prose", 62 advice-bearing messages unsampled), so the audit is manual. ROUTE #212 -- SEV-1, DEMONSTRATED AND LEFT OPEN WITH ITS PRICE. Route #205s shape for CLASS INVARIANTS. Owner module: `#@ class invariant self.v >= 0` over a class whose `sink()` sets `self.v = -5`; compiled alone it FAILS, correctly. An IMPORTER of that class PROVED `#@ ensures \result >= 0` for `c = C(); c.sink(); return c.v` (both with and without --deep), while CPython answers -5 and the TRUE twin `\result == 0 - 5` was REFUSED in the same importer -- the full decisive signature. The invariant rides along as a type invariant on the imported record and nothing in the importing unit discharges it. COMMANDS: owner $SCRATCH/p272/invmod.py, importer $SCRATCH/p272/invuse.py, twin $SCRATCH/p272/invtwin.py, run with `--memory-model hoare --deep --import-path $SCRATCH/p272`. Single-file carrier committed as 1721 (XFAIL). WHY IT IS OPEN RATHER THAN CLOSED: the two cheap repairs are both wrong. Refusing every import of an invariant-bearing class breaks legitimate multi-file programs (0441, 0443 do exactly that, and the corpus census found only 6 such importers, so the blast radius is small but the RULE is still wrong). Dropping the invariant from imported records weakens every honest importer. The right fix is route #205s -- re-emit the obligation where it is believed -- which for an invariant means re-proving PRESERVATION for each imported method, and that needs the method BODIES, which the importing unit deliberately does not lower (that opacity is the point of the import boundary). So the honest repair is a MODULE-LEVEL verification certificate ("this import was verified"), which does not exist in the IR today: there is no provenance field on an IR function at all (checked while measuring route #204s byte-diff). PRIORITY: this is the sharpest open route in the ledger -- it needs no trusted marker, no unusual annotation and no flag, only two ordinary files.

STRENGTHENS #212 and shows it is far wider than class invariants. THE SAME HOLE WITH NO CLASS, NO INVARIANT AND NO `#@ interface`: owner module `#@ requires \length(a) >= 1 / #@ assigns \nothing / def touch(a): a[0] = 5` FAILS compiled alone (frame violation, correctly). An importer doing `x = a[0]; touch(a); return x - a[0]` under `#@ ensures \result == 0` PROVED. CPython: -4. So route #204s repair (interface frames) closed a NARROW SPECIAL CASE of a WIDE hole: the importing unit believes EVERY contract of an imported module -- frames, postconditions, class invariants -- and nothing checks that the module was ever verified. TWO ORDINARY FILES, no annotation tricks, no flags. THE FIX IS A MODULE-LEVEL CERTIFICATE, not another per-clause re-emission: #205s move (re-emit the obligation where it is believed) works for an `#@ interface` because the goal needs only CONTRACTS, and does NOT work for a frame or an invariant because those need the BODIES the import boundary deliberately does not lower. Recorded as OPEN with that price. MEANWHILE THE ASSUMPTION IS BEING MEASURED FOR THE REPOS OWN POPULATION: 30 distinct LOCAL modules are imported by the corpus, and a sweep is verifying each one, so "the imported module was verified" becomes a checked fact here even while it stays an assumption in general.

Route #212s hole cannot be closed by re-emitting obligations (frames and invariants need the BODIES the import boundary deliberately does not lower), so the mechanism it actually needs was BUILT: `--verify-imports`, OFF BY DEFAULT so no existing run or byte output changes. It resolves each import with the shipping `_resolve_module_path`, verifies the module in a subprocess with the same flag (so verification is TRANSITIVE), carries a seen-set through the environment (PYCSL_VERIFIED_IMPORTS) so a cycle terminates and a diamond is verified once, and refuses with PYCSL-SEM-IMPORT-UNVERIFIED naming the module that failed. MEASURED: the dishonest pair (owner `#@ assigns \nothing` over `a[0] = 5`) is SUCCESS without the flag and PIPELINE ERROR with it; the honest pair (`#@ assigns a[0]` / `#@ ensures a[0] == 5`) is SUCCESS both ways. Corpus witnesses 1722 (XFAIL) and 1723 (PASS) run WITH the flag via their own `# pycsl-flags:` line, and the two dependencies live in multi_file_lib as r212_unverified.py (intentionally unverifiable, documented DO NOT FIX) and r212_verified.py. Route #212 stays OPEN because the flag is opt-in: the DEFAULT still believes every imported contract. Making it default is a policy decision (it re-verifies every dependency on every run of every importer) and is recorded as the next step rather than taken unilaterally. A module can be meaningful only inside an importing context, so a module-level certificate cannot simply mean "this file verifies on its own" -- which is exactly why `--verify-imports` must stay OPT-IN rather than becoming the default, and is the design note for whoever closes #212.
